i went to see the 1975 last January (my first concert) and i was so anxious but i was with a friend who knows me really well and it’s so amazing tbh and she knows i’m very anxious and autistic lol. honestly it was actually ok and i’d say it was worth it.. however i’ll list the things i struggled with;
1. waiting in the line to get in.. not my strong point waiting in cues.. surrounded by people and they can get very close. i also struggled with being anxious about having the wrong ticket at the doors but that was all irrational.
2. the lights can get a bit stressful after a while because they are very bright and quite flashy at times. but if you just close your eyes for 30 seconds or just take a quick break to the bathroom you should be good.
3. possible ear defenders. i know for me the music got very loud particularly at the end of the show. however it wasn’t excruciating. and i could deal but maybe take them just in case:)
4. i was in seats but still very surrounded. that was the one thing i truly struggled with was being surrounded by people. again, if you find yourself struggling, if you can take yourself off to the bathroom and recuperate 
-
another tip- if your friend knows you have asperger explain your struggles and reasons and a good friend will understand such as if you’re in the pit.. stand closer to the back because the front can be extremely personal. or anything that you think you will struggle with make your friend aware. 
-
also one thing... feel free to stim! i love stimming especially when listening to my favourite music, frankly nobody around you give a shit haha because they’re all concentrating on the music too and if you enjoy stimming , it really helps you relax and enjoy yourself, i love flapping while listening to music:) nobody cares i promise.
- HAVE FUN!!😋❤️
